SUMMARY 
This report recommends that City Council approve the demolition of an existing building 
on a non-contributing property located at 1337 Queen Street West within the Parkdale 
Main Street Heritage Conservation District (PHCD) and approve the erection of a 
replacement building in accordance with Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act in 
connection with the City-led Parkdale Hub project. 
The proposed development is for the West Block of the Parkdale Hub project to erect a 
new 16-storey mixed-use tower with a 4-storey podium building that will include 
purpose-built affordable housing; and which will remain under ownership of the City. 
A heritage permit for the project was previously approved on June 24 and 25, 2026, by 
City Council. The current proposal is largely the same as the previous approval, but a 
change has been made to the height of the podium of the new building. The street wall 
height of the new podium building has been increased by 1.2m which means that it no 
longer matches the height of the adjacent contributing building at 1347 Queen Street 
West. It also does not include the 5.0m step back required by the PHCD Plan for any 
parts of the new building that are taller than the adjacent contributing property. 
Consequently, a new Section 42 approval under the Ontario Heritage Act is required. 
One of the objectives of the PHCD Plan is to conserve the consistent and continuous 
streetwall that characterises most of the PHCD but this section of south side of Queen 
Street West has neither a consistent nor a continuous street wall. Therefore, the 
proposed modest height increase for the podium of the new Parkdale Hub West Block 
development would not harm the character or appearance of the District or be contrary 
to the objectives of the PHCD Plan. As such staff have no concern with the lack of a 
step back of the top of the new podium building in this location.

BACKGROUND 
Site and Context 
The City is undertaking the revitalization and expansion of the Parkdale Hub, which 
consists of several different properties located between Cowan Avenue and Dunn 
Avenue on the south side of Queen Street West to provide new affordable rental 
housing, improved community facilities, and modernized public spaces. The properties 
are owned by the City of Toronto and will be occupied and operated in partnership with 
various City Divisions and designated non-profit housing partners. 
A City-initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment application for the 
development for the Parkdale Hub project was approved by City Council on November 
8 and 9, 2023. The Parkdale Hub involves three blocks: 
• The West and East Blocks will accommodate housing, including purpose-built 
affordable housing. 
• The Centre Block will accommodate the renovated Masaryk-Cowan Community 
Centre and the new Toronto Public Library Parkdale Branch. A Heritage permit 
application proposing alterations to the heritage buildings located within the Centre 
Block was approved by City Council in 2023. 
The subject property at 1337 Queen Street West is an interior lot located between Dunn 
Avenue and Cowan Avenue on the south side of Queen Street West and is identified as 
the West Block of the Parkdale Hub project. The property contains an existing one-
storey building. 
The development site is located within the PHCD and is identified as a non-contributing 
property within the HCD Plan; meaning that it does not support the overall cultural 
heritage values, character and integrity of the District. 
Adjacent Heritage Properties 
The Site is adjacent to two contributing properties within the HCD on the south side of 
Queen Street West. Two of properties that form part of the Parkdale Hub project are

also individually designated under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act (OHA). These 
comprise of: 
• 220 Cowan Avenue, a former curling club designed in 1898 by Darling & Pearson, 
now the Masaryk Cowan Community Recreation Centre (Individually designated 
under Part IV of the OHA) (Centre Block) 
• 1313 Queen Street West, Police Station #6 designed in 1931-1932 by J.J. 
Woolnough, City Architect, with K.S. Gilles and S.T.J. Fryer, now a community run 
arts space (Individually designated under Part IV of the OHA) (Centre Block). This is 
separated from the application site by a parking lot at 1325 Queen Street West. 
1347 Queen Street West (inclusive of 265, 267, 269, and 271 Dunn Ave, and 1345 
Queen St West), a 3-storey brick main street commercial building constructed circa 
1882. This is a noted as a contributing property in the HCD but is not part of the 
Parkdale Hub project. 
Development Proposal 
The proposal for the West Block includes the demolition of the existing building 
identified as a non-contributing property within the PHCD to provide new affordable 
rental housing, improved community facilities, and modernized public spaces. 
The application proposes a 16-storey mixed-use building with a four-storey podium 
containing residential uses and ground-floor non-residential space. Beginning at the 4th-
storey, the tower is set back 8 metres from the Queen Street West frontage, with 
additional upper-storey stepbacks of 11 metres at the seventh floor. 
The side yard setbacks for the new tower will be 7.5 metres on both sides. The rear of 
the West Block will extend to the southern property line and will be designed to 
incorporate an east-west pedestrian connection between Dunn Avenue and Masaryk 
Park by pulling in the ground floor. 
The proposal received approval by City Council in June 2026. Revisions were recently 
made to the proposal that triggered the need for further approvals as the proposal is not 
substantially in accordance with the previous approval as it no longer complies with 
policies 7.6.4 and 7.6.5 of the PHCD Plan. 
The revised proposal increases the height of the 4-storey podium building by 1.2m in 
order to increase the floor-to-ceiling heights within the ground floor community space. 
All other details of the scheme remain as those approved by City Council in June 2026. 
A separate minor variance application is also required for the proposed revisions. 
Heritage Planning Framework 
The Planning Act 
The Planning Act guides development in the Province of Ontario. It states that 
municipalities must have regard for matters of provincial interest. Section 2(d)

specifically refers to “the conservation of features of significant architectural, cultural, 
historical, archaeological or scientific interest” and 2(r) "to a built form that is well 
designed and provides for a sense of place." 
The Provincial Planning Statement (2024) 
The Provincial Planning Statement (2024) (the "PPS") provides policy direction 
province-wide on land use planning and development to promote strong communities, a 
strong economy, and a clean and healthy environment. It includes policies on key 
issues that affect communities, such as: 
• The efficient use and management of land and infrastructure. 
• Ensuring the sufficient provision of housing to meet changing needs including 
affordable housing. 
• Ensuring opportunities for job creation. 
• Ensuring the appropriate transportation, water, sewer, and other infrastructure is 
available to accommodate current and future needs. 
• Protecting people, property, and community resources by directing development 
away from natural or human-made hazards. 
• Conservation of cultural heritage and archaeology. 
The provincial policy-led planning system recognizes and addresses the complex inter-
relationships among environmental, economic and social factors in land use planning. 
The PPS supports a comprehensive, integrated and long-term approach to planning, 
and recognizes linkages among policy areas. 
The PPS is issued under Section 3 of the Planning Act and all decisions of Council in 
respect of the exercise of any authority that affects a planning matter shall be consistent 
with the PPS. Comments, submissions or advice affecting a planning matter that are 
provided by Council shall also be consistent with the PPS. 
Policy 4.6.1 of the PPS directs that “Protected heritage property, which may contain 
built heritage resources or cultural heritage landscapes, shall be conserved." 
“Conserved” is defined in the PPS as the identification, protection, management and 
use of built heritage resources in a manner that ensures their cultural heritage value or 
interest is retained. 
All decisions of Council in respect of the exercise of any authority that affects a planning 
matter shall be consistent with the PPS and shall conform with Provincial Plans. All 
comments, submissions or advice affecting a planning matter that are provided by 
Council shall also be consistent with the PPS and conform with Provincial Plans. 
Provincial Plans are intended to be read in their entirety and relevant policies are to be 
applied to each situation.

Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District Plan 
The property at 1337 Queen Street West is within the boundaries of the Parkdale Main 
Street Heritage Conservation District (PHCD) Plan. The PHCD Plan works to protect the 
character of the District, conserve existing heritage attributes and resources, and guide 
future development. The subject property is identified as 'non-contributing' within the 
PHCD, meaning that it does not support the overall cultural heritage values, character 
and integrity of the District. 
The heritage attributes of the PHCD include: 
• Its historic main street character with its continuous streetwall and fine-grained built 
form 
• The consistent historic streetwall, fine-grained streetscape pattern and human scale 
of the District defined by predominantly 2 to 3 storey buildings 
The PHCD Plan's objectives include conserving the historic main street character of the 
District, including its consistent streetwall, scale and fine-grained built form. 
The following policies of the PHCD Plan have guided the review of the subject 
application: 
7.4.1 The demolition of buildings or structures on non-contributing properties may be 
permitted, upon satisfaction of policy 7.4.2 of this Plan. 
7.4.2 If permission to demolish a building or structure on a non-contributing property is 
granted, demolition activity shall not begin until plans for the replacement building(s) or 
structure(s) have been submitted and approved by Toronto City Council, and a heritage 
permit issued by the City. 
• (a) Ensure that the replacement building(s) conform to applicable policies 
contained in Sections 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 of this Plan, as well as the Official Plan 
and applicable zoning by-laws. 
• (b) Substantial progress should be made in the construction of the replacement 
building(s) or structure(s) within two years of the demolition of the previous 
building or structure.

7.5.3 New development and additions to non-contributing properties shall not negatively

COMMENTS 
A heritage permit for the project was previously approved on June 24 and 25, 2026, by 
City Council. The current proposal is largely the same as the previous approval, but a 
change has been made to the height of the podium of the new building. The street wall 
height of podium has been increased by 1.2m which means that it no longer matches 
the height of the adjacent contributing building at 1347 Queen Street West. It also does 
not include a 5.0m step back for all portions of the new building that are taller than the 
adjacent contributing building as required under Policies 7.6.4. and 7.6.5  of the 
Parkdale HCD Plan. Consequently, as the proposal does not meet these policies, a new 
Section 42 approval under the Ontario Heritage Act is required. 
One of the objectives of the HCD Plan is to conserve the historic main street character 
of the District, including its consistent streetwall, scale and fine-grained built form. There 
is however, no continuous or consistent streetwall along this part of the south side of 
Queen Street West. Therefore, although not strictly complying with policies 7.6.4 and 
7.6.5 of the PHCD Plan, the proposed modest increase in height of the 4-storey podium 
building will not negatively affect the legibility or prominence of the low-scale streetwall 
character along Queen Street West As such, the revised proposal continues to support 
the objectives of the HCD Plan. 
Staff note that, even with the proposed 1.2m. in height that is currently proposed, this 
scheme would introduce a more consistent streetwall condition along this part of the 
south side of Queen Street West than currently exists. 
Demolition and Construction - 1337 Queen St W Page 8 of 17

Staff also note that there is a reduction to the horizontal alignment in the revised 
proposal with the adjacent contributing property at 1347 Queen Street West when 
compared to the original design. Nevertheless, the articulation of the new four-storey 
podium continues to establish a streetwall design that responds to and is compatible 
with the horizontal and vertical organization, proportions, and rhythm of the contributing 
property at 1347 Queen Street West. The podium incorporates strong horizontal datum 
lines at the tops of the first- and fourth-floor windows, aligning with the adjacent signage 
band and roofline of this abutting contributing property. The façade composition further 
reflects the established pattern of storefront expression and upper-storey organization 
exhibited by the neighbouring heritage building, creating a compatible relationship while 
remaining distinguishable as contemporary construction. As a result, the podium 
reinforces and enhances the District's heritage main street character through the 
introduction of a fine-grained built form where such a condition does not currently exist 
along this portion of Queen Street West. 
The proposed materials, stepbacks and design of the new building remain unchanged 
and includes limestone coloured brick cladding and a storefront design on the ground 
floor. This allows the subject new building to be distinguishable and compatible with the 
red brick cladding used on the buildings located at 1313 and 1347 Queen Street West. 
The new tower above the 4-storey podium building meets the stepback requirement 
under policy 7.6.4 of the HCD Plan 
Staff are of the opinion that the proposed revisions to the building massing remain 
compatible with the adjacent contributing properties and continue to achieve the intent 
and objectives of the HCD Plan. 
CONCLUSION 
Staff recommend approval of the heritage permit application for the demolition of the 
existing building on the non-contributing property to facilitate the construction of a new 
16-storey mixed-use tower with a 4-storey podium for the West Block of the Parkdale 
Hub project. 
The revised design of the building is considered compatible with that of the adjacent 
heritage buildings and staff consider that the application conserves the cultural heritage 
values of the PHCD. As such Heritage Planning staff are of the opinion the proposal is 
consistent with the objectives of Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District 
Plan. It is therefore recommended that City Council approve the application under 
Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
